title: SPACE-BASED SERVICES FOR WATER SCARCITY - KS
description: Water is one of the most important substances on Earth and covers 70% of the planet. However, every year competition for a clean, copious supply of water intensifies. Fresh water is threatened by a myriad of forces including overdevelopment, polluted runoff and global warming. Space applications can help to alleviate water scarcity problems in numerous ways. The "Water Scarcity" Kick Start offers 75% funding of up to 60,000 EUR for teams to explore the technical and commercial feasibility of a new service tackling issues related to water scarcity. Proposed services can address one of the following topics: planning and monitoring desalination plants, addressing groundwater depletion, digitising the water and wastewater industry, reducing water loss during distribution, improving water harvesting, optimising purification applications, and supporting new farming techniques that use less water. The services put forward must use at least one type of space asset, such as Earth observation, Satellite Communication, or Satellite Navigation technology.

title: 81314609-Consultancy services for the project Strong Water Utilities in Jordan
description: The Jordanian water sector plays a critical role in the nation"s development, serving as a vital resource for agriculture, industry, and domestic sides in the country. At a share of around 9% , the water sector is one of Jordan's largest single consumers of electricity, and the trend is rising. The energy cost is considered one of the big challenges as it is made up around half of the operation and maintenance cost of water and wastewater services in the sector . High rates of drinking water loss (over 50%), which can be traced back to combination of illegal use and connections on supply networks, vandalism and leakage , increase the pressure on water resources and significantly reduce the economic efficiency of the Jordanian water sector. Not forgetting the effects of climate change will significantly reduce the available water resources over the next 20 years (15% by 2040). There are more than 1,000 water (pumping stations, water treatment plants, lifting stations, desalination plants, and wells) and wastewater facilities in the sector, distributed across the country with operational responsibility for these facilities distributed under three main Water Utilities (WU"s) (Yarmouk in Northern governorates, Miyahuna in middle governorates and Aqaba in Southern governorates), around 47% of these facilities are covered by Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) which is considered the main source of master data (energy, water, and operational data). While it is planned to reach 100% coverage within coming 3 years, dealing with data within the sector is still a major challenge! Whether dynamic or static, end-to-end data journey from its sources (field meters and sensors), to transmitting it by local RTU or PLC through communication channels (wired, wireless or even satellite) to SCADA centers, store it and process it in various database and finally interpret data according to used system by the end user (Operational by SCADA or technical by enterprise resource planning (ERP)). This paly a vital role in the efforts of standardized and state-wide anchoring of NRW processes and energy management. GIZ acknowledges the different dimensions of Jordan"s water sector challenges. Consequently, German development cooperation will continue to offer support through short and medium-term oriented activities as well as long-term oriented measures aiming at efficient management of water resources to secure the future water supply of the country. The scope of work will be divided into three main work packages, where each package targeted specific items (total of 5 sites: three water companies, water authority of Jordan and Jordan valley authority). WP 1 - titled "Water loss reduction (non-revenue water)", aims to institutionalize processes to reduce water losses in the responsible units of the ministry of water and irrigation and the Water Utilities (WU"s). WP 2 - titled "Sustainable Energy Management (ISO 50001 EnMS)" aims to institutionalize energy management in the energy units of Water Authority of Jordan and WU"s. WP 3 - titled "Improving Wastewater treatment operation", aims to improve the basis for the operation of wastewater treatment plants in terms of environmental compatibility and technical standards.

title: T709-814GD HUMAN-MACHINE INTERACTION TECHNOLOGY EXPLORATION AND USE CASE ASSESSMENT FOR MISSION OPERATIONS (EXPRO+)
description: Data generated by missions is increasing and at the same time, more spacecraft are being monitored and controlled by ever fewer operators to maintain an efficient business model. Operators face the task to monitor a growing number of parameters per spacecraft anda substantially increased cognitive effort of controlling entire fleets in the future. While automation helps to reduce the number of interventions, the fact remains that operators need to be able to efficiently interpret the information presented to them and actfast and correct in case their intervention is required.The human-machine interaction technology in current ground systems (simpleuser interfaces) had been designed to present as much unfiltered information as possible, reflecting a now outdated operations conceptwhere multiple specialized operators would monitor a single mission. Continuing to add more information within the same interfaces is reaching the limits of what operators can safely monitor. In recent years the field of human-machine interaction technology (adiscipline lying in intersection of computer science, cognitive science, and human-factors engineering) has made giant leaps forward, driven by the innovation in other industries (e.g. entertainment). Clean and supportive user interfaces with minimal complexity are common features that are required for user-friendly interfaces. Therefore, the objective of the activity is to leverage advancements made in HMI technology and assess their spin-in potential to improve efficiency in mission operations interfaces.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Create as-is report of operator user interfaces with a gap assessment against state-of-the-art HMI technologies, identifying technology gaps and outlining use cases based on typical operations activities. Specific attention is given to reduction of the operators cognitive load exposure. The technology development shall be agnostic with regards to the underlying ground data system- Detailed assessment of the identified use cases- Develop software mock-ups / prototypes to substantiate usecaseassessment. Prototypes are to address also key objectives such as operational efficiency (should there be a need, implement hardware components).- Assess the results against potential synergies with other technologies, for example in the field of AI (digital assistants) and automation to be explored further in a future activity- Develop a reference architecture and roadmap for spin-in and adoption of HMI technology into mission operations
